summary.text: Creates the
`application.handle`

content.text:
The host calls the handler only after device, route, capability and optional
product admission succeeded. The handler records the admission, then removes
the device transport headers
`authorization`
`cookie`
and
`origin`

and the
proxy headers
`forwarded`
`x-forwarded-*`
and
`x-real-ip`

from both
the parsed and raw header views, so the application never mistakes a device
credential for its own authentication and never re-evaluates the already
verified LAN origin. The original request and response streams are passed on
unchanged otherwise. The admission is released exactly once, on response
finish, response close or context abort. A synchronous dispatch error, or a
rejection of a returned promise, releases the admission and is rethrown to the
host, which then reports the failure. An already aborted context is refused
without admission or dispatch.
A handler suitable for
IRemoteApplicationAdapter.handle

content.text:
The caller remains responsible for local authorization: invoke this handler
only for requests already proven to come from the application's own local
administration surface, never for device requests admitted by the remote host.
Route every request whose path equals or begins with the prefix here and pass
the original, unconsumed request whose
`url`
is the complete origin-form target.
`GET <prefix>/status`
returns the status.
`POST <prefix>/enable`
`/disable`
`/reconcile`
and
`/revoke`
run their command and return the resulting status;
`POST <prefix>/pair`

returns the secret-bearing invitation, which must only be
shown locally. Write bodies are strict JSON (
`{ "endpointId"?: string }`
`{ "deviceId": string }`
), parsed by
parseRemoteHostControlCommand

.
Queries, trailing slashes and unknown paths yield 404; a wrong method yields
405 with
`Allow`

; non-JSON or invalid bodies yield 422; a declared or streamed
body above the limit yields 413 and closes the connection;
`forbidden`

yields
403; a missing control, full command queue or unavailable host yields 503.
Every response is
`no-store`
; JSON responses use
`application/json`

, and
error bodies carry only
`{ error: { code, message } }`
Resolves after the command completed and its response was submitted.
RemoteProtocolError with
`invalid-request`

for an invalid prefix or body limit; command, validation
and host failures are written as HTTP errors instead. A response that can no longer carry an error is destroyed.

content.text:
The wrapped host remains the sole authorization, listener and persistence
owner. Every command runs in one bounded queue (default 16 running or queued
operations); a failed command never blocks later ones. Nothing polls and no
timer is created: the network interface is rechecked when access is enabled,
before every pairing invitation and on an explicit reconcile command. An
availability failure of a lifecycle command (initialize, enable, disable or
reconcile) is retained and projected through
RemoteHostRuntime.status

without terminating the application; the next successful lifecycle command
clears it. Refused pairings and revocations are the caller's result and never
change the retained availability. The application must await
RemoteHostRuntime.dispose
before closing services the host dispatches to.

aborts. Entries are held weakly and never extend a request's lifetime.
